system.name: FlashMem
system.one_liner: a memory-streaming framework that reduces memory use and latency for large-scale and multi-DNN inference on mobile GPUs

components.name: Disk
components.role: on-device storage holding DNN weights before loading

components.name: UM
components.role: unified memory that first receives weights streamed from disk

components.name: TM
components.role: texture memory holding weights reorganized into 2.5D tiled layout

components.name: L2
components.role: shared L2 cache between unified memory and the streaming multiprocessors

components.name: SM0
components.role: streaming multiprocessor executing DNN compute, reading through its Texture Cache

components.name: SM1
components.role: second streaming multiprocessor, symmetric to SM0

components.name: Texture Cache
components.role: per-SM cache exploiting 2D spatial locality of texture memory

components.name: Preemptible pool
components.role: multi-DNN strategy where a high-priority model can interrupt or replace a lower-priority one in execution

components.name: FIFO queue
components.role: multi-DNN strategy where models are queued and executed sequentially, the strategy FlashMem targets

flows.what: weights transformed into 2.5D texture memory layout
weights consumed during execution via the Texture Cache

content.key_idea: mobile GPU inference pays a multi-step disk-to-UM-to-TM-to-SM weight transfer cost, and this cost repeats for every model when multiple DNNs are run FIFO-style, motivating FlashMem's streaming approach
content.reading_order: left panel (a) top-to-bottom follows the numbered weight-transfer path from disk through UM and TM to the SMs; right panels (b) and (c), stacked below the 'Input' label, contrast preemptible versus FIFO multi-DNN scheduling

palette.used_for: SM / Texture Cache / UM blocks in the mobile GPU memory hierarchy

style.arrows: thin orthogonal and slightly curved arrows tracing the numbered weight-transfer path
style.icons: vector icons representing small DNN graphs (nodes/edges) queued in the preemptible pool and FIFO queue

encoding.color_means: distinct pastel fills separate the mobile-GPU memory-hierarchy blocks (blue/purple) from the multi-DNN scheduling illustrations (pink for preemptible, orange for FIFO)
encoding.emphasis: circled step numbers (1, 2, 3) trace the costly multi-hop weight path in panel (a), directly motivating why panel (c)'s FIFO scheduling repeats that cost per model

summary: FlashMem targets efficient execution of large and multi-DNN workloads on mobile GPUs by streaming weights instead of fully preloading them. Figure 1 sets up the motivation in three panels. Panel (a) shows the hierarchical mobile-GPU memory system -- Disk, Unified Memory (UM), Texture Memory (TM), L2 cache, and per-SM Texture Caches feeding SM0/SM1 -- with three numbered steps tracing how weights move from disk into UM, are reorganized into 2.5D texture layout in TM, and are finally consumed during execution on the streaming multiprocessors. Panels (b) and (c), under a shared 'Input: images, audio, texts...' label, contrast two multi-DNN support strategies: a preemptible pool where a high-priority model can interrupt another, and a FIFO queue where models execute strictly in sequence. The figure is a dense, square-cornered block diagram using pastel color blocks and small DNN-graph icons to keep the memory hierarchy and the scheduling comparison visually distinct.
summary_zh: 该图分三部分呈现动机：(a) 展示移动 GPU 存储层次（磁盘、统一内存UM、纹理内存TM、L2、SM及纹理缓存）及权重经三个编号步骤传输执行的路径；(b)(c) 对比两种多DNN调度策略——可抢占池与FIFO队列，说明FlashMem所针对的重复加载开销问题。
